title: pH Meter Calibration

references.label: General microbiology/molecular biology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: To verify and adjust a pH meter's readings against certified standard buffers before use, ensuring subsequent pH measurements are accurate.
principle: A pH electrode's response can drift over time due to aging, contamination, or temperature changes; calibration against at least two standard buffers bracketing the expected working range establishes the correct slope and offset for the meter to apply to raw electrode readings.
requiredMaterials: Calibrated thermometer (if the meter does not have automatic temperature compensation)
requiredReagents: At least two certified pH calibration standard buffers bracketing the expected sample pH (commonly pH 4, 7, and 10)

procedure.instruction: Rinse the electrode with purified water and gently blot (not wipe) dry.
Immerse the electrode in the first calibration standard (commonly pH 7) and allow the reading to stabilize before confirming/accepting the calibration point per the meter's instructions.
Rinse the electrode again, then repeat with a second standard bracketing the expected sample range (e.g. pH 4 for acidic samples or pH 10 for alkaline samples).
For a three-point calibration, repeat with the third standard.
Rinse the electrode one final time before beginning sample measurements.
Record the calibration date, standards used, and any displayed slope/offset value for quality documentation.

observations: The meter accepts each calibration point within its expected tolerance and reports a slope value within the manufacturer's acceptable range.
interpretation: A successful calibration with an acceptable slope value indicates the electrode is responding correctly across the tested pH range; a slope far outside the acceptable range, or difficulty stabilizing on a standard, suggests the electrode may need cleaning, reconditioning, or replacement.
criticalNotes: Always rinse (not wipe with a dry tissue) the electrode between standards to avoid cross-contaminating the buffers.
Recalibrate at the start of each use session, or per the facility's defined schedule — do not rely on a calibration from a previous day.
precautions: Never let the electrode's sensing bulb dry out; store it in the manufacturer-recommended storage solution between uses.
limitations: Calibration standards themselves have a shelf life and can degrade once opened or contaminated — using an expired or contaminated standard produces a false calibration.
